components.css: .ds-entry-demo { width:min(420px,100%); } .ds-entry-button { position:relative; z-index:1; isolation:isolate; width:100%; min-height:56px; padding:0 28px; overflow:visible; color:#0505a9; font:800 14px/1.2 Inter,system-ui,sans-serif; letter-spacing:.035em; text-transform:uppercase; background:transparent; border:0; border-radius:30px; transition:color 500ms ease,transform 180ms ease; cursor:pointer; } .ds-entry-button::before { position:absolute; z-index:3; inset:0; content:""; border:2px solid #0505a9; border-radius:30px; pointer-events:none; } .ds-entry-label { position:relative; z-index:2; } .ds-entry-inner { position:absolute; z-index:0; inset:0; overflow:hidden; background:#fff; border-radius:30px; } .ds-entry-blobs { position:relative; display:block; height:100%; filter:url(#ds-entry-goo); } .ds-entry-blobs > span { position:absolute; top:2px; width:25%; height:100%; background:#0505a9; border-radius:100%; transform:translate3d(0,150%,0) scale(1.4); transition:transform 450ms ease; } .ds-entry-blobs > span:nth-child(1) { left:0; } .ds-entry-blobs > span:nth-child(2) { left:30%; transition-delay:80ms; } .ds-entry-blobs > span:nth-child(3) { left:60%; transition-delay:160ms; } .ds-entry-blobs > span:nth-child(4) { left:90%; transition-delay:240ms; } .ds-entry-button:hover,.ds-entry-button:focus-visible { color:#fff; transform:translateY(-1px); outline:0; } .ds-entry-button:hover .ds-entry-blobs > span,.ds-entry-button:focus-visible .ds-entry-blobs > span { transform:translateZ(0) scale(1.4); } .ds-entry-button:focus-visible::before { box-shadow:0 0 0 4px rgb(5 5 169 / 16%); } .ds-entry-filter { position:absolute; width:0; height:0; pointer-events:none; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce) { .ds-entry-button,.ds-entry-blobs > span { transition:none; } }

narrative.overview:
The Dispatch Console treats the interface as a calm, dependable operations room: Dispatch Navy anchors the shell, Signal Blue identifies action and active state, and Console Mist keeps dense administrative data readable for long sessions. The system is professional and specific to metro work, using route discs, status signals, operational labels, tables, and live-state cues instead of decorative dashboard tropes.

Routine screens stay compact and decisive, with precise spacing, restrained interaction, and a clear progression from page heading to summary, filters, and records. Visual intensity is reserved for meaningful state and exceptional entry moments; the login may become more expressive, while the working console remains quiet enough for scanning and decision-making.
keyCharacteristics: Dark Dispatch Navy navigation paired with bright, low-noise work surfaces.
Compact Inter typography with small uppercase operational labels and firm numeric emphasis.
Signal Blue reserved for action, selection, focus, and information—not ambient decoration.
Thin dividers, quiet tonal layering, and restrained shadows supporting dense data.
Metro-specific status discs, route markers, tables, and operational language.

rules.name: The Signal, Not Spectacle Rule
rules.body: Signal Blue marks action, selection, focus, and useful information; it does not wash entire routine screens in color.

rules.name: The Status Has Meaning Rule
rules.body: Green, amber, and red always communicate operational state and must be paired with text, icons, or labels rather than color alone.

rules.name: The Compact Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Dense screens use small labels and restrained body text, but page titles, key values, and actions must remain immediately distinguishable.

rules.name: The Operational Horizon Rule
rules.body: Preserve scan lines, aligned controls, and readable records; collapse structure by priority instead of shrinking dense content past usability.

rules.name: The Layered Operational Rule
rules.body: Borders and tone do the everyday structural work; strong shadows appear only when a surface genuinely moves above the console.

rules.name: The Soft, Not Playful Rule
rules.body: Corners reduce visual friction, but geometry remains compact, aligned, and task-oriented rather than bubbly or ornamental.

rules.name: The Routine vs. Entry Rule
rules.body: Routine work uses quiet, rectangular controls; expressive motion and the blob capsule belong only to exceptional entry moments.

dos: Do preserve the Dispatch Navy shell, Console Mist canvas, and white operational surfaces as the stable hierarchy.
Do use Signal Blue consistently for primary action, active navigation, focus, and useful information.
Do keep status color semantic and reinforce it with readable labels or icons.
Do preserve compact tables, aligned toolbars, and responsive priority-based collapse.
Do reserve expressive gradients and the animated blob treatment for brand and entry moments.
donts: Don't turn the console into a futuristic neon or cyberpunk control room.
Don't use excessive glassmorphism, exaggerated gradients, or pervasive translucent cards.
Don't default to a generic card-heavy SaaS dashboard when a table, route marker, status signal, or operational panel is more specific.
Don't repeat the blob button across routine create, save, filter, or row actions.
Don't visually imply that Metro NY is an official MTA product or reproduce an official identity it does not own.
